  Guide to City Council Proceedings

Meetings of the City Council are held the first and third Tuesday of each month at 9:00 a.m. and
are conducted in accordance with Rosenberg's Rules of Order (Vernon Municipal Code Section
2.1-1).

Copies of all agenda items and back-up materials are available for review in the City Clerk
Department, Vernon City Hall, 4305 Santa Fe Avenue, Vernon, California, and are available for
public inspection during regular business hours, Monday through Thursday, 7:00 a.m. to 5:30
p.m. Agenda reports may be reviewed on the City's website at www.cityofvernon.org or copies
may be purchased for $0.10 per page.

Disability-related services are available to enable persons with a disability to participate in this
meeting, consistent with the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA). In compliance with ADA, if
you need special assistance, please contact the City Clerk department at
CityClerk@ci.vernon.ca.us or (323) 583-8811 at least 48 hours prior to the meeting to assure
arrangements can be made.

The Public Comment portion of the agenda is for members of the public to present items, which
are not listed on the agenda but are within the subject matter jurisdiction of the City Council. The
City Council cannot take action on any item that is not on the agenda but matters raised under
Public Comment may be referred to staff or scheduled on a future agenda. Comments are limited
to three minutes per speaker unless a different time limit is announced. Speaker slips are
available at the entrance to the Council Chamber.

Public Hearings are legally noticed hearings. For hearings involving zoning matters, the
applicant and appellant will be given 15 minutes to present their position to the City Council.
Time may be set aside for rebuttal. All other testimony shall follow the rules as set for under
Public Comment. If you challenge any City action in court, you may be limited to raising only
those issues you or someone else raised during the public hearing, or in written correspondence
delivered to the City Clerk at or prior to the public hearing.

Consent Calendar items may be approved by a single motion. If a Council Member or the public
wishes to discuss an item, it may be removed from the calendar for individual consideration.
Council Members may indicate a negative or abstaining vote on any individual item by so
declaring prior to the vote on the motion to adopt the Consent Calendar. Items excluded from the
Consent Calendar will be taken up following action on the Consent Calendar. Public speakers
shall follow the guidelines as set forth under Public Comment.

New Business items are matters appearing before the Council for the first time for formal action.
Those wishing to address the Council on New Business items shall follow the guidelines for
Public Comment.

Closed Session allows the Council to discuss specific matters pursuant to the Brown Act,
Government Code Section 54956.9. Based on the advice of the City Attorney, discussion of
these matters in open session would prejudice the position of the City. Following Closed
Session, the City Attorney will provide an oral report on any reportable matters discussed and
actions taken. At the conclusion of Closed Session, the Council may continue any item listed on
the Closed Session agenda to the Open Session agenda for discussion or to take formal action
as it deems appropriate.

SUBJECT
Proclamation Recognizing the Grand Opening of the Southern California Curling Center in Vernon

Recommendation:
Acknowledge and present a proclamation in recognition of the Grand Opening of the Southern California
Curling Center.

Background:
On April 7, 2020 the City Council adopted Ordinance No. 1264, approving and authorizing the execution
of a development agreement with The Southern California Curling Center, Inc. for the development of a
dedicated curling facility in the City. The first of its kind in California, the now complete 42,000 square
foot custom built facility boasts the most sheets of dedicated curling ice west of the Dakotas.

Positioned to become a premier facility for competitors at all experience levels, from the newly inducted
to the elite world champion, the Southern California Curling Center is a dedicated curling facility that will
allow for year-round opportunities to grow and promote the sport. Southern California Curling Center is
the new home of Hollywood Curling, a 501 (c)(3) non-profit curling club dedicated to advancing the sport
of curling in Southern California and is also the U.S. home of the Mexican Curling Federation.

From adaptive curling to youth, the Southern California Curling Center strives to make curling accessible,
especially for those not yet part of the curling community, and invites everyone to experience the
community and enjoyment that comes from curling. Through its partnership with curling clubs and
organizations such as Hollywood Curling and the Mexican Curling Federation, as well as the programs
offered at the facility including youth curling, adaptive curling, and Learn to Curl events, the Southern
California Curling Center provides a unique and enriching experience for the local community.

As part of the Business Appreciation & Recognition Program, the City welcomes the Southern California
Curling Center to Vernon and will participate in its Grand Opening festivities with a ribbon cutting
ceremony on August 28th at 5:00pm.

Fiscal Impact:
The cost associated with this item is minimal and was included in the current fiscal year budget as part of
funds earmarked for the City's Business Appreciation & Recognition Program.

SUBJECT
Recognition of Retired Employee - Adam A. Alvarez, Street Maintenance Worker, Lead

Recommendation:
Acknowledge and present a proclamation to retired employee Adam A. Alvarez, Street Maintenance
Worker, Lead, in recognition of his dedicated service to the City of Vernon.

Background:
Historically, the City Council has issued proclamations in honor of retired City Employees. Adam A.
Alvarez, Street Maintenance Worker, Lead, retired from the City of Vernon on July 29, 2021 after
providing over thirty-four (34) years of service to the City.

Adam Alvarez was hired as a Utilityman V effective July 1, 1987. During the course of his employment
with the City of Vernon, he held the following positions: Utilityman IV effective July 2, 1989, Utilityman III
effective July 1, 1990, Street Maintenance Worker, Senior effective April 20, 2014, and Street
Maintenance Worker, Lead effective March 17, 2019.

Adam Alvarez can be recognized for many accomplishments during his long career with the City of
Vernon. On June 25, 1998, Mr. Alvarez assisted a Vernon community member after she had been
robbed. He promptly relayed important identifying vehicle information to the Vernon Police Department,
leading to the arrest of four suspects. Adam Alvarez lead the 2019 Public Works Department projects
that modified accessibility to City-owned housing. He also designed the recent street island upgrades
and lead the Citywide street island beautification project for the 2020-2021 fiscal year. Over the course
of his tenure, he completed hundreds of hours of training and seized countless professional development
opportunities.

During his distinguished career with the City of Vernon, Adam Alvarez has won the deepest respect of
his colleagues through his leadership and dedication to the Public Works Department. Adam A. Alvarez
was an instrumental member of the street maintenance team and lead many public works construction
projects throughout the City, he will truly be missed. Adam Alvarez was hired on July 1, 1987 and meets
the eligibility requirements under CalPERS to retire from the City of Vernon effective July 29, 2021.

Fiscal Impact:
There is no fiscal impact associated with this report.

SUBJECT
Presentation on Pension Obligation Bonds

Recommendation:
No action required by City Council. This is a presentation only.

Background:
Pension costs have historically been one of the largest sources of expenditures for local government;
furthermore, after the 2008 Great Recession, CalPERS experienced substantial losses in its portfolio’s
value and implemented several reforms that have contributed to increased costs to the City to address
the unfunded liability. In an effort to address these pension related costs, staff is actively engaged in
identifying options that best serve the City’s needs and obligations long-term.

As such, on June 22, 2021, the City of Vernon entered into a licensing agreement with GovInvest (a
pension, Other Post-Employment Benefits (OPEB), and labor Software-as-a-Service solution and
consulting firm) for use of their proprietary Pension Obligation Bond Module and related services
included in the software agreement to: 1) Analyze the benefits and risks associated with issuing bonds to
refinance pension and OPEB debt; and, 2) Help develop alternative funding approaches for current and
future pension and OPEB debt and analyze the benefits and risks associated with each of the
approaches. GovInvest will present its findings to Council, focusing on the potential savings, risks, and
benefits of issuing Pension Obligation Bonds.

There is no fiscal impact associated with this report.

SUBJECT
Amendment No. 2 to the Services Agreement with Southeast Area Animal Control Authority (SEAACA)

Recommendation:
Approve and authorize the Mayor to execute Amendment No. 2 to the Services Agreement with
SEAACA for animal control services to update the schedule of fees effective July 1, 2021.

Background:
On July 2, 2019, the City of Vernon and SEAACA entered into a five-year agreement (July 1, 2019 to
June 30, 2024) for animal control services. The agreement provides for annual costs and fees for animal
control services in accordance with the established schedule of fees. The agreement stipulates that the
established schedule of fees may be adjusted annually by mutual agreement of the parties. On July 1,
2020 the City of Vernon and SEAACA entered into Amendment No. 1 updating the schedule of fees for
FY 2020-2021. The proposed Amendment No.2, effective July 1, 2021 updates SEAACA's schedule of
fees for FY 2021-2022 as follows:

Field Officer Service, per hour - $81.42 to $85.73
Shelter of live animals per animal, per day - $11.00 to $15.00
Special holding, quarantine impounds, per animal, per day - $33.37 to $50.00
Veterinary medical services, per impound - $61.80 to $75.00
Impoundment of livestock, per animal - $90.00 to $94.77

The $95.00 fee for Use of special equipment, per hour category will remain the same.

To ensure continuation of services, the Department of Health and Environmental Control recommends
approval of the amendment. The amendment has been reviewed and approved as to form by the City
Attorney's Office.

Fiscal Impact:
Approval of this amendment will result in a fee increase in five out of the six fee categories. Sufficient
budget is available in the current agreement to cover the cost associated with the increase in service
fees.

SUBJECT
Public Works Department Vehicle Purchase

Recommendation:
Approve the purchase of two (2) new 2022 Chevrolet Silverado 2500HD 4WD Crew Cab Work Trucks
through National Auto Fleet Group, for a total cost of $91,334.02.

Background:
The Fiscal Year (FY) 2021-2022 budget for the Public Works Department’s (Department) Building
Maintenance and Garage divisions includes planned capital expenditures for the purchase of two new
trucks to meet the operational needs of the Department. The purchase of these new vehicles will provide
Public Works staff the transportation necessary to continue to promptly execute daily work
responsibilities and effectively meet the needs of the City.

The City of Vernon is a member of Sourcewell, formerly the National Joint Powers Alliance, which offers
members cooperative buying contracts. Pursuant to Vernon Municipal Code Chapter 2, Article IV,
Section 2.17.12(A)(5), the purchase of the proposed vehicles is exempt from the City conducting its own
competitive bidding, as Sourcewell’s practice ensures that members receive the lowest price available
using its competitive bidding process. The quote secured for this purchase is with a company that sells
equipment based on a Sourcewell contract. It is to the advantage of the City to procure these vehicles
from the selected vendor. The quote provided by Sourcewell indicates cost savings of $15,059.22 based
on the Manufacturer’s Suggested Retail Price (MSRP). Staff recommends the approval of the purchase
of two new 2022 Chevrolet Silverado 2500 HD 4WD Crew Cab Work Trucks through National Auto Fleet
Group, for a total cost of $91,334.02.

Vernon Municipal Code 2.17.02(B), requires City Council approval if, in the twelve (12) months
preceding the effective date of a proposed new, renewed, or otherwise amended contract, the City has
paid or awarded the vendor more than $100,000. In Fiscal Year 2021/2022, the City has awarded the
National Auto Fleet Group a total of approximately $685,653.54.

Fiscal Impact:
The Department has budgeted for the trucks to be purchased from the FY2021-22 budget. Funds will be
expensed from accounts 011.1046.900000 and 011.1049.900000.

SUBJECT
Blanket Purchase Contract with The Home Depot

Recommendation:
A. Find that the best interests of the City are served by a direct award of a blanket Purchase Oder to The
Home Depot without a competitive selection process pursuant to Vernon Municipal Code (VMC) Section
2.17.12 (b)(2); and
B. Approve the issuance of a blanket Purchase Order with The Home Depot in an amount not-to-exceed
$150,000 to procure supplies for Public Works and VPU for operational needs and special projects for
Fiscal Year 2021-22.

Background:
The Public Works Department (Public Works) and Vernon Public Utilities (VPU) purchase various
supplies to meet City operational needs. Typically, both departments make such purchases from The
Home Depot (Home Depot) and each fiscal year blanket Purchase Orders are established to facilitate
necessary purchases. Staff is requesting that the City Council find that the best interests of the City are
served by a direct award of a blanket Purchase Oder to Home Depot, as this vendor is the nearest to the
City with the inventory and breath of products and equipment desired by the City. Other vendors in the
area do not offer the breath or quantity of products available through Home Depot, thus utilizing an
alternative vendor for select products would result in additional trips and time incurred by City staff in
locating/purchasing necessary supplies. Although there may be vendors with comparable inventory,
pricing and variety located further from the City, it would be time consuming and inefficient for staff to
procure supplies from those vendors, as much time would be lost in transit.

During FY2020-2021, Public Works initiated several special projects requiring increased spending on
supplies. Specifically, Public Works special projects include street island improvements, City Hall
beautification, and the remodel of two (2) City-owned residential properties. These projects are all still
ongoing. Staff anticipates a need for increased spending to continue in FY2021-2022, as Public Works
is making a conscious effort to utilize staff on special projects and reduce spending on outside
contractors whenever possible. The remodel of the City-owned residential property located at 3361
Fruitland Avenue was managed by the Facilities division, and while this resulted in overall cost-savings to
the City, it also required increased spending at Home Depot to procure the materials needed.

Per Vernon Municipal Code 2.17.02(B), City Council approval is required if, in the twelve (12) months
preceding the effective date of a proposed new, renewed, or otherwise amended contract, the City has
paid or awarded the vendor more than $100,000. Within the past twelve (12) months, the City has paid or
awarded Home Depot a total of approximately $104,515.02. Additionally, staff has purchased materials
using their credit cards totaling approximately $13,561.93.
 In order to ensure that both Public Works and VPU staff is able to procure materials and supplies
necessary for their operational needs and special projects for Fiscal Year 2021-2022, staff is requesting
the approval of a blanket purchase order in an amount not-to-exceed $150,000.

Fiscal Impact:
If approved, the cost of supplies will be charged to Public Works and VPU accounts accordingly.

SUBJECT
Purchase of Electric and/or Hybrid Vehicles for City Departments

Recommendation:
A. Approve the purchase of three (3) electric vehicles to replace the existing Department of Health and
Environmental Control (DHEC) fleet vehicles, and approve the purchase of one (1) additional electric
vehicle to serve as the City designated vehicle for the Director of DHEC for a total cost not to exceed
$153,571;
B. Authorize a 10% contingency amount of $15,357 in the event that it is necessary for the DHEC to
secure similar vehicles from alternate dealers should the vehicles quoted no longer be available for sale;
and
C. Authorize the purchase of one (1) plug-in hybrid vehicle to replace the existing vehicle designated for
City Council use at a not-to-exceed amount of $45,000 from a dealer offering a competitive price.

Background:
The Department of Health and Environmental Control (DHEC) vehicle fleet is overdue for replacement
and continuously experiences maintenance issues. As the recycling coordinator for the City of Vernon,
the DHEC must take an active role in building a model for environmentally sustainable City management
and, as such, the DHEC has opted to procure electric fleet vehicles. The Department’s Fiscal Year (FY)
2021-2022 budget includes planned capital expenditures for the purchase of three new electric vehicles
to replace the current gas vehicles used by staff to conduct mandated inspections, complaint
investigations, and emergency response. The DHEC conducts inspections at approximately 1,200
facilities in the City of Vernon, annually engaging with business operators.

The City of Vernon is a member of Sourcewell, formally the National Joint Powers Alliance, which offers
members cooperative buying contracts and typically makes vehicle purchases through Sourcewell.
Pursuant to Vernon Municipal Code Chapter 2, Article IV, Section 2.17.12(A)(5), vehicle purchases are
exempt from competitive bidding since Sourcewell's practice ensures that members receive the lowest
price available using competitive bidding. However, due to the severe inventory shortage of vehicles
(electric vehicles in particular), the City has not been able to secure vehicles from Sourcewell. The City is
also experiencing challenges when attempting to purchase directly from dealers, as electric vehicles are
being sold rapidly, not providing the City an opportunity to request approval for the purchases while
specified/quoted vehicles remain in stock. Overall, electric vehicle inventory in the region is extremely
sparse at this time, with little to no options available from which to select specific makes and models.

The DHEC is requesting approval to purchase three (3) electric fleet vehicles for staff and one (1) vehicle
to be used by the Director of Health and Environmental Control pursuant to the City’s Citywide Fringe
Benefits Policy. The Department expects to spend approximately $153,571, which is an estimate based
on the quotes provided for three (3) Nissan Leaf electric vehicles and one (1) Ford Mach E electric
vehicle. The DHEC will attempt to procure the vehicles quoted, however, staff anticipates that challenges
may arise because of the aforementioned widespread inventory issues. Thus, the DHEC is requesting
 the flexibility to secure vehicles of similar makes and models from alternate dealers should the vehicles
detailed in the quotes no longer be available for sale. Furthermore, the DHEC is requesting approval of
a 10% contingency fund, in addition to the $153,571 anticipated purchase price, as the vehicle prices
may fluctuate if the DHEC must purchase vehicles from an alternate dealer and/or purchase different
makes and models.

Based on the lack of inventory and challenges noted above with regards to the purchase of electric
vehicles, staff is also requesting flexibility in the purchase of a plug-in hybrid vehicle for use by the City
Council, as there may not be sufficient time to seek authorization once a quote is secured. By
authorizing a not-to-exceed amount for this type of vehicle, Council will allow staff to shop for the most
competitive offering in available inventory. At this time, there is no availability for a reasonably priced
plug-in hybrid vehicle. However, when making a purchase, the Finance Department will ensure that staff
adheres to the City’s purchasing processes.

Fiscal Impact:
The expenditure for the purchase of the DHEC vehicles is approximately $153,571 and shall not exceed
$168,928 (which includes a 10% contingency amount of $15,357). The expenditure for the purchase of
the City Council vehicle shall not exceed $45,000. Funds for the vehicle purchases are available in the
Health Department and City Council budgets respectively for FY 2021-22.
